Fiscal austerity, with and without monetary offset

For nations in the "Monetary Policy Zone," the author claims that

fiscal austerity seems to have no effect. This is exactly what the market monetarists predicted, but conflicts with the prediction of the Keynesian model.

Fine, but there is a huge world of other things going on here. These countries are not in any "Zone." The use of this term is an attempt to make the "monetary" nations more comparable to each other and to minimize acceptance Keynesian economics. In other words, this is an argument working from the conclusion backwards. In fact, these countries are far more random in terms of economies than the nations in the first two graphs, which share more common cultures and economies.

In the end, the author proves Keynes correct but fails to prove anything new about monetary policy. Maybe that's why he complains that "Keynesians simply ignore" these reports. How many times should economists continue to discredit bad reports? Monetary policy had already failed as an overall system before its original theoretical formulation was completed!

More realistically, fiscal policy has its place at the center of macroeconomic analysis. Monetary policy has its place in certain areas.

Those who continue to try to prove monetary policy central do so for ideological purposes. All the charts and graphs and highly-polished pinpointed and complex analyses are not going to change this -- but they get the lay people believing it. That's the main purpose.
